target_customer: Enterprises that want no-code AI agents for back office workflows such as compliance audits, legal intake and claims underwriting
problem: Building and governing LLM powered workflows across enterprise systems took engineering teams months.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscription with services-led deployments

founders.name: Antoni Rosinol
founders.background_notes: Listed as Toni Rosinol on the YC page.

founders.name: Bernardo Aceituno
founders.background_notes: Listed as Bernard Aceituno on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating LLMs with enterprise connectors and governance is standard engineering with security work, and founders had MIT research backgrounds.

defensibility.rationale: Many visual LLM builders appeared at once; integrations and enterprise deployments provided some lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform vendors shipped agent builders, but StackAI was bought by Asana in May 2026 instead.

market_need_then: Interest in LLM apps surged after late 2022, and enterprises sought no-code ways to deploy them; no dated spend figure found.

branding.domain_note: Uses stackai.com on the current site and has used stack-ai.com; a crypto project also uses StackAI, so the name is shared. Domain purchase history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, repeated demo prompts; tagline The Enterprise AI Agent Factory

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name with a name collision, but it kept the brand after the Asana deal and the sale shows enterprise recognition.

outcome_analysis: StackAI caught the enterprise agent wave, raised a small seed then a 16 million dollar Series A in 2025, signed customers such as Monzo and BAE Systems, and was bought by Asana in May 2026 for a price outlets put at 75 million dollars but the parties did not confirm. Strong founders and an enterprise motion drove a mid sized exit while competition from platforms kept the standalone path hard.
notes: Seed date conflict: company blog dated 21 May 2024, aggregators say April 2023; recorded as 2024-05. Series A date conflict: company blog May 2025 versus CB Insights December 2024; recorded as 2025-05. Series A amount 16M seen in company post and several outlets; PitchBook via a trade outlet says total under 20M. The 75M purchase price is reported by many outlets but not confirmed by the companies, so amount_usd is null. No dated competitor sources near the W23 batch were found (results were 2026 comparison pages), so the list is empty.
